name: Standing calf raise
cue: Sink into a deep stretch, pause, and stay in the bottom half.
research: research.json biomech.calf_raise: balls of the feet on the block edge, heels free, knees ~3 deg (straight, never bent), hips and trunk neutral, hands on the pad handles; research range ankle 25 deg dorsiflexion -> 30 deg plantarflexion. Drawn range: the bottom half, after Jeff Nippard (feel a deep stretch at the bottom, do not go all the way up onto the toes): 25 deg dorsiflexion (heels well below the block) -> 3 deg plantarflexion (heels about level with the forefoot), with a 1.5 s pause in the stretch (tempo: lift 1.0, top 0.2, lower 2.0, stretch 1.5 s). Block 0.055 H (~10 cm) tall so the heels drop ~8 cm below its surface at the stretch without reaching the floor. Rolling contact: the toe joint (metatarsal-head line) is pinned just over the block's rear edge and the toes stay flat on the block (toe ext = -dorsiflexion), so the foot rolls about the metatarsal heads; the body rises ~8 cm and drifts ~3 cm forward (~13.7 and ~5 over the full range). The shoulder pads ride on a lever that pivots above and behind the lifter (hub placed for the full range; the bottom half uses the lower part of the same arc). The rolling foot alone would carry the pads on an arc that bulges backward mid-rise while the lever arc bulges forward, so the rigid lever would have to stretch by up to 2.6 cm (at the new top); instead, as on a real machine, the lever sets the path and the whole body pitches forward about the toe line by up to 1.15 deg (1.14 at the top; via keys M1-M5 and the top key, toes kept flat; tools/design/calf_raise_link.mjs), which keeps the lever length constant to the millimetre. Muscles: gastrocnemius only (research primary, medial head reaching lower than the lateral). The soleus (research secondary) lay directly under the gastrocnemius and read as a tan sock that touched the primary, with no chip of its own, so it is not drawn. Load: a cam on the far lever hub winds a cable that runs down the far post to a guided weight stack; it rises about 4 cm as the lever turns over the rep. (tools/design/loads.mjs)

skinChecks.note: forefoot stays on the block through the loop
heels hang free above the floor plate, deepest at the stretch
